clue.text: Ready to run about wildly in training

indicators.note: in places the frolicking word inside the abbreviation for training

parts.note: to romp is to run about boisterously

explanation.surface: Someone eager to charge around excitedly during a fitness session.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt as an adjective means quick to act, ready and punctual.

clue.text: Learner endlessly begging to carry doctor's coat

indicators.note: to carry means the shortened pleading word holds the doctor inside it
endlessly means the word for pleading loses its final letter

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A trainee who won't stop pleading is made to bring along the doctor's overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' looks like a garment in the surface but is the skin of a young animal; MB (Bachelor of Medicine) is the usual crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lambskin is a garment or hide from a young sheep, worn as a coat.

clue.text: Beneath the waves dunes are shifting

indicators.note: shifting sands move about, so these letters of the dunes phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sand dunes move about under the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Undersea describes something located below the surface of the ocean.

clue.text: Places frequented by husband and relatives?

explanation.surface: Spots a married man and his family members visit often.
explanation.definitionFit: Haunts are favourite spots that someone visits habitually.

clue.text: Former music academy, one serving seasoned beef

parts.note: RAM is the Royal Academy of Music in London
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ex-conservatoire student now works serving spiced meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is smoked, highly spiced cured beef.

clue.text: A bloke holding peacekeepers to be plentiful

indicators.note: holding means the slang word for a man has the peacekeepers inside it

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or bloke

explanation.surface: A man hosting UN troops finds supplies are ample.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound means to exist in large numbers, to be plentiful.

clue.text: Lively wife overwhelmed by choral performance

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the wife letter is engulfed inside the choral word

explanation.surface: A spirited wife is drowned out by the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging means lively and fashionable, as in the swinging sixties.

clue.text: Again decorate European in Republican party

indicators.note: in places the European letter inside the political and party pieces

explanation.surface: A European attending a Republican party wants the place redecorated.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo a room is to paint or decorate it afresh.

clue.text: It was once played extremely regularly in the centre

indicators.note: in the centre means the letters are taken from the very middle of the two words

explanation.surface: Something formerly played very often at the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The eighteen letters of 'extremely regularly' have this four-letter run exactly at their centre, extreme-LYRE-gularly.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is an ancient stringed instrument played in classical Greece.

clue.text: Branch of trade leaderless Brahmans maybe attempt to follow

indicators.note: to follow means the attempt comes after the shortened group
leaderless means the first letter of the religious group is removed

parts.note: Brahmans are an example of Hindus, the priestly caste

explanation.surface: Hindu priests without a head try to follow a business sector.
explanation.definitionFit: An industry is a particular branch of commercial or manufacturing activity.

clue.text: Structure of a block of fired clay that's been trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed means the phrase loses its two outer letters

parts.note: a brick is a block of fired clay

explanation.surface: The structure of a clay brick that has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the wordplay: OFABRICK, trimmed at both ends by 'that's been trimmed', loses O and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric means the basic framework or structure, as in the fabric of society.

clue.text: One that makes an all-out effort to collect leaves?

definitions.text: One that makes an all-out effort to collect leaves?

parts.words: One that makes an all-out effort to collect leaves
parts.note: reads as a hard trier, but really a kitchen sieve that catches tea leaves while pouring

explanation.surface: Someone working flat out to gather leaves, like a gardener in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is one who strains hard, and also the sieve used to catch tea leaves.

clue.text: A stubborn beast ultimately without charm

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An obstinate animal that is utterly lacking charm.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil.

clue.text: Beyond belief, sacking councillor unfit for course!

indicators.note: sacking means the councillor is dismissed, removed from the word

explanation.surface: Unbelievably, a councillor is fired over an unfit racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' means a course of a meal, not a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Food not fit to be eaten as a course of a meal is inedible.

clue.text: Supplier of milk and chips — a Scot possibly

parts.note: fries is the American name for chips
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A dairy supplier sells chips, perhaps run by a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Friesian is a breed of black-and-white dairy cow, a supplier of milk.

clue.text: Talk idly about source of this river flowing west

indicators.note: in an across clue flowing west means the whole run is read right to left
source of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: Chatting idly about where this river begins as it runs westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing west' turns RETTAY back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To yatter is to chatter idly and at length.

clue.text: Like English barn let out?

indicators.note: out means these letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A farm building in England offered for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: Rentable means able to be let out for payment, as a barn might be.

clue.text: Majestic West Tower primarily used for opening fair?

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress

indicators.note: used for opening means the letter goes into the fair word, splitting it
primarily means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grand western tower is mainly used to open a fete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a funfair but means so-so.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is a musical direction meaning to be played in a majestic, stately manner.

clue.text: Antipodean army's obsession with ending of action

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force, here with its possessive s

indicators.note: ending of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone from down under shares the army's obsession with getting results.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania lies south of Australia, so a Tasmanian is an Antipodean.

clue.text: Who shall be principal first violin? Me?

definitions.text: Who shall be principal first violin? Me?

parts.words: Who shall be principal first violin? Me?
parts.note: an orchestral player asking who will lead the orchestra, slyly angling for the job, is posing a question that steers toward a desired answer

explanation.surface: An ambitious violinist hopes to be chosen as orchestra leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In British orchestras the principal first violin is called the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading question prompts the answer the questioner wants, here a question about leading.

clue.text: Fellow clutching a speaker's gift turned over large cushion

indicators.note: clutching means the man's name holds the article inside it

parts.note: Ben is a man's name, standing for any fellow

indicators.note: turned over means the speech word is read backwards

parts.note: gab, as in the gift of the gab, is fluency in speech

explanation.surface: A man holding an orator's present tipped onto a big cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanbag is a large soft cushion filled with beans or pellets, used as a seat.

clue.text: Be acquainted with friar unknown in Derby area

parts.note: Friar Tuck of the Robin Hood legend

explanation.surface: Knowing an anonymous friar in the English town of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is an English city, but the Kentucky Derby is the famous US horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky is the US state where the Kentucky Derby is run.

clue.text: Dramatic fall of eastern lad brought up above seedy bar

indicators.note: above means the first part sits over the bar in the down entry
in a down clue brought up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar

explanation.surface: An eastern youth raised above a sleazy pub suffers a big fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep plunge, figuratively a dramatic fall.

clue.text: Dishonour that is terrible at first in strictly Labour environment?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation and initial inside the phrase for the political setting

parts.note: a strictly Labour place has no Tory in it
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: at first means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A disgrace that's terrible, at first, in a solidly Labour area.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour and the Tories (Conservatives) are rival British parties, so a strictly Labour place has NO TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is being famous for something bad, a kind of dishonour.

clue.text: Play jazz before service, with noisy rabble

parts.note: to riff is to play a jazz phrase
the RAF is a British armed service
f, forte, means loud in music

explanation.surface: Jazz played before a church service, with a rowdy mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests church but is the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Riffraff means disreputable people, the rabble.

clue.text: Sail away taking girl round part of Africa

indicators.note: round means the girl's name goes around the other pieces

explanation.surface: Setting sail with a girl to go around Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Hammerstein, possibly? It's Cyril for a change

indicators.note: for a change means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is Cyril the man behind the musical's words, as a change?
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Hammerstein II wrote the words for Rodgers' musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammerstein was a lyricist, writer of song words, so he is an example.

clue.text: Vicar takes drug repeatedly, transfixed by rough wake-up call

parts.note: Rev, Reverend, is a vicar's title

indicators.note: transfixed by means the illness word pierces through the pair of drug letters
repeatedly means the drug letter appears twice

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes drugs over and over, pierced by a rude awakening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfixed by' runs ILL through EE, giving EILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning.

clue.text: Frozen state of cape south of here in France

indicators.note: in a down clue south of means the headland goes below

parts.note: a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: An icy state south of here, in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Iciness is the condition of being frozen with ice.
